NoteTexAccessor::citations¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::citations() const

Extract One Argument Per Citation Command¶

citations() finds \cite-family commands and returns each command’s required brace argument as one token. The family includes letter-suffixed and starred forms such as \citep, \citet, and \citet*. Any number of optional square-bracket notes between the command and required argument are accepted and omitted from the result.

The unit of extraction is the citation command, not the individual key. A source command \cite{a,b} therefore yields the single token a,b. This is useful when command grouping and author-supplied key order matter. Choose bibliography_keys() when each comma-separated key should become an independent token and \bibitem declarations should also participate.

Matches preserve source order and occurrence count. A malformed command, a missing required group, or a required group containing nested braces is ignored. The method does not expand macros, resolve keys against a database, or suppress commands inside comments; compose with strip_comments() first when comments are outside the desired source domain.

The return value follows the closed TokenBatch contract: tokens() is the flat rank-1 Text payload, while Int64 offsets() maps every flattened source cell to its half-open token interval. Cells without citations repeat the previous offset. Undefined yields undefined tokens and offsets [0]. Non-Text Notes reject. Extraction does not mutate the receiver and costs a source scan plus storage for matched arguments and offsets.

Example 1: Grouped Keys, Two Optional Notes, And A Starred Form¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\cite{a,b} \citep[see][p. 4]{c,d})", R"(\citet*{e})",
    "no citation"});
const auto citations = source.tex().citations();

std::cout << citations.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["a,b", "c,d", "e"]

Example 2: Offsets Preserve Command Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = citations.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3]

Example 3: Native Integer Cells Reject¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().citations();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "citations Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

citations Int64: rejected
